newsitem.title: USA: No meeting planned between Clinton, Fujimori.
newsitem.headline: No meeting planned between Clinton, Fujimori.

text.p: The White House made it clear on Friday that President Bill Clinton has no plans to meet with Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori next week.
U.S. officials said, however, that Fujimori will be offered a meeting with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.
Fujimori arrived in Toronto on Friday for talks with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on ending Lima's 45-day-old hostage crisis. Fujimori is scheduled to stop in Washington early next week.

Peruvian officials had said earlier this week that Fujimori would meet Clinton on Monday to thank him for his backing during the Lima hostage crisis, but on Friday a senior Peruvian official conceded such a meeting was now unlikely.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Peru had not requested a meeting and doubted Clinton could fit Fujimori into his schedule.
"The president of the United States doesn't have drop-by visits," he said, adding that Clinton had taken a low-key posture on the hostage crisis on the advice of his counter-terrorism experts.
McCurry said Fujimori was scheduled to meet Assistant Secretary of State for Inter-American Affairs Jeffrey Davidow.
He said the United States "highly values his views" and was looking forward to having an exchange with Fujimori.
The senior Peruvian official said that Fujimori "will attend a forum of foreign investors in Latin America in Washington on Sunday and on Monday a session of the United Nations."
